items.title: HFCL bags export orders worth ₹834 crore for optical fibre cables
items.summary:
Telecom gear maker HFCL on Thursday said it has secured export orders worth about Rs 834.36 crore (around USD 88.94 million) for supplying optical fibre cables to an international customer, through its overseas wholly-owned subsidiary.
The order is scheduled for completion by June 2027.
The company, however, did not disclose the identity of the customer.
"These orders reaffirm the confidence reposed by our customers in the company's manufacturing capabilities, technological excellence and product quality," HFCL said in a regulatory filing.
HFCL posted a multi-fold jump in consolidated profit to Rs 394.22 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from Rs 72 crore a year ago, driven by demand for optical fibre cables from AI data centres.
The company has forecasted 80 per cent revenue growth in FY27 and expects to achieve the Rs 10,000 crore revenue mark before the projected timeline of FY29.
HFCL's consolidated revenue from operations more than doubled to Rs 2,541.7

items.summary: IIFL Finance shares rallied as much as 4.90% to hit an intraday high of Rs 657.70 during Wednesday's trading session after the company announced a Rs 6,414 crore ($686 million) primary capital infusion led by global investment firm Blackstone and its promoters.The proposed fundraise is among the largest primary private equity investments in a listed Indian non-banking financial company (NBFC).In a regulatory filing, IIFL Finance said its board, at a meeting held on November 10, approved the capital raise through a preferential issue.Blackstone Private Equity will invest Rs 5,000 crore ($535 million) through a preferential allotment of compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS). These shares will convert into equity shares at Rs 602 apiece, in line with the regulatory pricing, within 18 months of allotment.Meanwhile, the company's promoters, Nirmal Jain and R. Venkataraman, will invest Rs 1,264 crore ($135 million) through a preferential allotment of warrants. Anchorage Capital will also participate in the transaction with a primary equity investment of Rs 150 crore ($16 million).The company and its promoters have entered into definitive agreements with Blackstone and Anchorage Capital for the proposed transaction, which remains subject to customary regulatory and shareholder approvals.According to  IIFL Finance,  the capital infusion will strengthen its capital adequacy, lower its cost of funds and accelerate growth in its gold finance business, a secured retail lending segment.The proceeds will also support IIFL Finance's ambition to emerge as one of India's largest diversified retail NBFCs.The company aims to tap Blackstone's global network and expertise in operations, technology, data and AI to expand its secured lending businesses, attract talent and strengthen its market position.The proposed appointment of Blackstone representatives to the company's board is also expected to enhance governance standards and oversight.Welcoming the investment, founder and Managing Director of IIFL Finance Nirmal Jain said the partnership would provide the company with additional capital to expand its businesses, invest in technology and deepen co-lending partnerships with banks while maintaining a disciplined approach to risk and capital.Also read: Kalyan Jewellers shares surge 10% to hit upper circuit on strong Q2 earningsIIFL Finance share price performance and Technical indicatorsIIFL Finance shares have gained around 11% over the past week. The stock currently commands a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 26,838 crore. Its 52-week high stands at Rs 705.On the technical front, Trendlyne data shows that the stock is trading above all eight of its simple moving averages (SMAs), indicating strength across these moving-average indicators.Disclaimer: The views/recommendations mentioned in this article, wherever applicable, are those of the respective SEBI-registered Research Analyst/brokerage and have been reproduced/reported with due attribution. Centre's EV push puts electric mobility stocks in the fast lane; M&M, Ola Electric lead rally with gains of up to 5%
items.summary: Shares of automobile and electric vehicle companies gained on Wednesday, November 11, following the Centre's decision to make electric vehicles the default choice for staff-car procurement by government ministries and departments, while doubling the Net Dealer Price (NDP) ceiling for electric cars to Rs 20 lakh. Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) and Ola Electric Mobility emerged among the top gainers in the sector, with the former leading the rally with an intra-day gain of nearly 5%.M&M climbed 4.81% to touch an intra-day high of Rs 3,449, while Ola Electric Mobility advanced 3.53% to Rs 35.16.Hyundai Motor India was another major gainer, rising 3.08% to an intra-day high of Rs 2,175, while TVS Motor Company gained 2.89% to Rs 4,636.10. Ather Energy advanced 2.40% to Rs 1,904.50.Among other automobile companies, Maruti Suzuki India rose 2.10% to Rs 13,199, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles gained 2.03% to Rs 301. JBM Auto advanced 2% to Rs 511.95, while Bajaj Auto registered the lowest gain among the nine stocks, rising 1.28% to Rs 11,120.At the last check, M&M was trading 4.5% higher, followed by TVS Motor Company, which was up 2.53%. Ola Electric Mobility gained 2.20%, while Hyundai Motor India advanced 2.3%. Maruti Suzuki India was up 2%, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Ather Energy gained 1.5% each. Bajaj Auto and JBM Auto were trading 0.5% higher each, while Ashok Leyland was flat.ALSO READ: Earnings recovery, FII revival: 5 factors that will shape Dalal Street's next move after Q2What does the Centre's new EV procurement policy say?The Department of Expenditure (DEA), under the Ministry of Finance, has revised the Net Dealer Price (NDP) ceiling for the procurement of staff cars by government ministries and departments, doubling the limit for electric vehicles to Rs 20 lakh from Rs 10 lakh for internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.Under the revised instructions, electric vehicles have been made the default choice for government staff-car procurement. Ministries and departments are directed to ordinarily procure EVs when purchasing or replacing their existing staff cars.However, the revised instructions do not completely prohibit the purchase of conventional vehicles. Departments that consider EV procurement or deployment impractical can propose purchasing ICE vehicles, subject to justification and case-specific relaxation from the Department of Expenditure, with the required approvals.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.summary:
Adani Enterprises Ltd plans to spend between Rs 35,000 crore and Rs 40,000 crore annually over the next couple of years, with airports, data centres and its proposed PVC complex emerging as the biggest investment drivers as the conglomerate steps up expansion across its infrastructure businesses.
"We expect to do capex at a run rate of around Rs 40,000 crore. So, we may be somewhere in the range of Rs 35,000 crore to Rs 40,000 crore, which is the rate we expect to continue over the next couple of years," Manan Vakharia, head of finance at Adani Enterprises, said during the company's earnings call.
The planned spending comes as the group seeks to scale up businesses built over recent years, including airports and data centres, while bringing its large manufacturing investments closer to commercial operation.
"The heavy lifting will be done by airports, data centres and PVC," Vakharia said.
